comparison: Perfect agreement on transcriptome quality assessment (C57-C61). Both evaluations find the assembly metrics, read counts, BUSCO completeness, and annotation success demonstrate high-quality data suitable for downstream analyses.

Perfect agreement on positive selection findings (C93-C96, C130-C131). Both evaluations support the use of multiple methods to detect positive selection and accept the finding that male-biased genes show ~10% higher proportion of positively selected genes compared to other categories.

Perfect agreement on relaxed selection findings (C97-C98, C149-C150). Both evaluations accept the RELAX model results and the connection to gene duplication as a mechanistic explanation for relaxed selection patterns.

Perfect agreement on codon usage bias analysis (C100-C103). Both evaluations accept the finding that male-biased genes have stronger codon bias and higher dS values, which provides alternative explanation for elevated ω values.

Strong agreement on sex-biased expression patterns (C3, C62-C63, C67-C68, C71). Both evaluations support the 15-fold difference in sex-biased genes between floral buds and mature flowers, with all reviewers explicitly acknowledging this core finding.

Strong agreement on faster evolution of male-biased genes (C5, C81-C84, C87-C89). Both evaluations strongly support this central finding using two-ratio and free-ratio models, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming appropriate methods and consistency of data.

Perfect agreement on novelty claim (C9, C129). Both evaluations confirm this is the first report of faster-evolving male-biased genes in plants, with all reviewers explicitly recognizing the novelty of this finding.

Divergent evaluations on sex-linkage analysis (C152-C154). OpenEval finds the analysis appropriately addresses confounding factors and supports the interpretation. Peer Reviewer 2 identifies this as a weakness requiring further investigation, though authors addressed the concern.

Strong agreement on functional enrichment and adaptive evolution (C6-C7, C111-C114, C132-C133). Both evaluations support the KEGG pathway enrichment showing male-biased genes enriched in stress/immune pathways, though both note the inference of adaptive evolution is not definitively proven by enrichment alone.

Agreement on specific gene functions and sexual selection interpretation (C134-C135). Both evaluations accept the identification of genes involved in flowering time and pollen development, with appropriate caution about the speculative nature of sexual selection claims.

Agreement on unexpected pattern of more female-biased genes (C4, C120-C121). Both evaluations support this finding and accept the functional enrichment-based interpretation, though OpenEval notes it remains somewhat speculative.

Agreement on dual mechanisms of positive and relaxed selection (C110 vs C8). Both evaluations accept that both forces contribute to faster evolution of male-biased genes, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming this mechanistic interpretation.

Partial overlap on gene duplication mechanism (C8, C146-C148). OpenEval provides detailed theoretical framework and comparative examples. Peer review accepts the dual mechanism interpretation but does not separately evaluate the gene duplication theory.

Partial overlap on functional enrichment patterns (C124-C127 vs C112-C113, C122-C123). OpenEval integrates physiological and morphological observations with expression data. Peer review focuses on pathway enrichment without detailed evaluation of dimorphism claims.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty about 'feminization' interpretation (C64-C66), noting speculation and lack of consideration of alternative explanations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific clustering interpretation.

OpenEval supports overlap analysis between sex-biased and tissue-biased genes (C72-C78), finding males have higher tissue-bias. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific analysis.

OpenEval supports findings for flowers at anthesis (C85-C86, C90-C92), noting appropriate caution about low statistical power and inconsistent results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this developmental stage.

OpenEval supports intensified selection findings using RELAX model (C99), with consistency across multiple methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found separately addressing intensified selection.

OpenEval supports overlap analysis between high evolutionary rate genes and tissue-biased genes (C141-C145), finding small overlap and low constraints. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific analysis.
